title: 2027 Forensic FOI, Records Recovery and Institutional Accountability Programme
purpose: Repeat and materially improve the 2026 disclosure and records-recovery campaign, reconstruct the wider Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr / Llandough-juxta-Penarth / Leckwith record landscape, resolve every unanswered question, and pursue proportionate institutional accountability where evidence supports it.
method: PRINCE2-style staged management: continued business justification, defined roles, management by stages, management by exception, product focus, tailored controls and lessons learned.

requester_closures.meaning: Requester-initiated closure; not an institutional non-response or missed deadline. Preserve earlier clock and outcome history.

gmail_subject_search.meaning: Lower-bound thread-match estimate; includes notifications, follow-ups, withdrawals and duplicates, not a request count.

highlight_reports.hr06: 2026-10-22: 11 red houses, 9 red fish; 35 open send-email tasks checked; 19 already sent; 12 never sent and no longer in draft; remaining four require status reconciliation.
highlight_reports.hr07: Recorded OPEN in 2026-10-30 master report; final report and action closure still require reconciliation.
highlight_reports.monthly_governance: January–September monthly reports recorded no formally authorised work packages before 19 October, no Project Board, no agreed tolerances and no products completed. September was reconstructed retrospectively; October began Stage S0 with G0 forecast for 18 December, overall AMBER.
highlight_reports.unsent_internal_reviews: 28 September 2026: Wales Office and National Archives internal-review drafts recorded as not sent; National Archives 23 September disclosure not yet entered in the evidence library.

october_startup.tolerances: Not yet agreed by the Project Board
october_startup.cost: No actual spend asserted; external costs not yet quoted.

roadmap_2026.source: 21 Nov disclosure snapshot; targeted TNA and HMLR addendum from 24 Nov 2026. Remaining recipient lanes and static timelines require full source reconciliation.
roadmap_2026.note: 84 unique lane IDs across three split files; duplicate lane fragments combined by stable ID.

baseline_caveat: Datasets have different dates and denominators and must not be combined as one total. Tracker base through 18 October; request-status through 21 October; latest roadmap generated 24 November and as of 21 November; 6 November count is a historical snapshot. The 84 Dartboard roadmap lanes plus two additional recipient/parent lanes produce 86 2027 subprojects. Q&A source discovery, year-end Gmail reconciliation, HR-07 closure and 2026 carryover review remain mobilisation gates.
lessons_2026: Next-working-day inbox triage; routine draft/review target one working day.
Follow-up was not systematic: next-day acknowledgement checks, due-date reminders and first-working-day-overdue chases are mandatory.
Cross-thread and cross-reference matching before concluding an answer is absent.
Publish as-of date, coverage boundary, refresh log and denominator with every metric.
Read and index every attachment before classifying a response as substantive.
Map record holders, regimes, aliases and question dependencies before drafting.
Use numbered question-by-question answer matrices.
Measure authority delay and requester delay separately.
No reply, late reply, changed wording or not-held statement is a lead for verification, not proof of motive.
Highlight reports require clear ownership, current snapshots, consistent denominators, reviewer capacity and closure of unsent tasks.
Preserve the 18 requester-initiated closures as separate statuses; do not erase historic clock results.
No work packages were formally authorised before 19 October 2026; the 2027 PID, Project Board, tolerances, stage plan and work-package authority must exist before delivery begins.
January–September reports recorded no Project Board and no agreed time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk or sustainability tolerances; establish these at the 2027 initiation gate.
Monthly reports repeatedly recorded no completed products; measure accepted products and evidence outcomes, not correspondence volume or activity.
The 28 September Wales Office and National Archives internal-review drafts were recorded as not sent; every draft now has an owner, review slot, due date and daily queue check.
The National Archives disclosure of 23 September was not yet entered in the evidence library; ingest and index every incoming record within one working day.
The National Archives search was widened after an initially narrow search; search by creator, company, litigation, registration, transfer, aliases and record series, not only the property name.
Museum Wales site-wide scope risked being narrowed to a single object; preserve the full question scope and record every proposed narrowing with reasons and approval.
A register-level conclusion is not proof of the underlying historical title; test it against the first-registration file, complete instruments, plans, objections and transfer records.
Separate information-rights handling from the underlying evidence question: a request may be answered while the historic record question remains open.
Contact-channel reliability is a risk: log bounced addresses, online-form redirects and portal-only requirements, then verify the replacement route before sending.
control_rules: Every inbound message triaged by next working day with owner and next action.
Every request has owner, independent reviewer, regime, due date or no-clock status, and next-action date.
Check for replies on the next working day after due date; chase the same day if absent.
Routine outgoing drafts target one working day; exceptions have owner, reason and recovery date.
Reminders at 5, 2 and 0 working days; first-working-day-overdue chase; assess escalation at 5 and 10 working days.
A response is not complete until all attachments are read, all numbered questions dispositioned and cross-thread replies checked.
Keep FOIA, EIR, SAR, archive enquiry, voluntary private-party request, regulator complaint and ombudsman complaint distinct.
Verify every recipient's own ladder and distinguish statutory, good-practice, discretionary, parallel and unavailable routes.
Requester withdrawal is not an institutional outcome; preserve earlier clock and decision history.
Record exact statement, date, source, contradiction and alternative explanation; do not label people dishonest.
No external email, formal complaint, legal filing or public allegation without required human authorisation.
No delivery work package starts until its product description, owner, reviewer, acceptance criteria, dependencies, tolerance and authority to proceed are recorded.
Every incoming disclosure and attachment is ingested into the evidence library within one working day, with stable evidence ID, source, date, version, page count and checksum where available.
No institution may narrow a site-wide or multi-record request to one object without a written scope analysis, requester decision where needed and independent QA.
No product is complete on administrative closure alone; completion requires the defined acceptance test and an evidential disposition.

governance.executive: Programme Executive — final authority for external action, public release, complaints, spend and legal decisions.
governance.project_manager: AI Project Manager — plan, schedule, dependencies, RAID, reporting and handovers.
governance.project_assurance: Independent QA agent(s), separate from drafter; challenge sources, scope, legal route, completeness and fairness.
governance.work_register: HubSpot private task/review register; GitHub Issues public-safe engineering ledger; Dartboard disclosure/failure marker; Projects programme view; Hive coordination and handover only.
governance.project_board: Executive, Senior User, Senior Supplier and Project Assurance roles are established at G0; decisions, tolerances, change control and stage-end approvals are minuted.
governance.tolerances: Set explicit time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability tolerances at G0; report forecast breach as an exception before the limit is crossed.

phases.name: Mobilise and reconcile
phases.exit: 2026 mailbox, Dartboard datasets, 84 roadmap lanes, HR-06/HR-07, Old Chestnut and Q&A sources reconciled; approved question register and 2027 baseline; live 2026 deadlines handed over. Signed PID/business case, Project Board, product descriptions, approved tolerances, stage plan, RAID/quality/lessons registers and authorised first-stage work packages.

phases.name: Forensic records mapping and question design
phases.exit: Each of 86 subprojects has verified records map, unresolved-question matrix, request sequence, legal route, retention/preservation map and QA-approved drafts.

phases.name: Disclosure and parallel archive recovery
phases.exit: Planned requests submitted and tracked; responses and attachments analysed; alternative holders searched; justified internal reviews started.

phases.name: Escalation and accountability
phases.exit: Every unresolved refusal, delay, search issue or service failure has a documented remedy decision and any justified complaint prepared/filed through the correct route.

phases.name: Closure, synthesis and year-end review
phases.exit: Every question answered or given a documented final disposition; institutional histories reconciled; lessons, year-end report and 2028 options approved.

tasks: Refresh all 2026 Gmail FOI/EIR/SAR/complaint threads, attachments, drafts and sent items through 31 December.
Reconcile the 260-thread tracker, 261-record request-status register, 318-conversation 6 November count and 84-lane roadmap without combining dates or denominators.
Reconcile HR-06 and HR-07; extract every open action, decision, risk and missed follow-up from the 2026 highlight-report series.

global_work_packages.name: Q&A unanswered-question closure
tasks: Verify the dedicated Q&A repository unclehowell/cedwyn-qa, deployed route, current release/build commit and source coverage.

Reconcile the 362-record Q&A Hall snapshot dated 19 October and the 23 October correspondence snapshot (304 requests, 406 questions, 467 replies) against the current live export; do not treat historical counts as current.
Verify the daily 04:17 UTC refresh workflow and last successful run; restore and validate static/qa/kb.json and static/qa/api/qa.json if the live export is missing or stale.

Export every Hall item and classify answered, partly answered, not held, refused, redirected, pending, no reply, contested, statement only or open; preserve exact wording, source references and stable IDs. The Hall's open-question count remains unknown until this export is recovered.

Import all 20 case questions (5 open, 5 family-account, 4 contested, 4 documented, 2 not-held) and all 7 research questions (5 open, 1 partly answered, 1 answered); review family-account and contested items for independent evidence.

Create one traceable QID task for each of the 10 explicit open questions below, link it to the relevant institution subprojects and source records, and preserve the 2 research follow-ups as separate statuses.
Resolve the discrepancy between the 14 November changelog's six research questions and the current seven-item JSON; retain the 23 November drainage-instruments addition.
Reconcile the Q&A Hall against Gmail and Dartboard; the refresh automation does not read Gmail, HubSpot, Hive or private drafts, so it is not a complete substitute for mailbox review.

global_work_packages.name: That Old Chestnut forensic accountability
tasks: Reconcile all six current Peekaboo observations against original requests, complete threads, later mail, attachments and actual records.
Classify each as later record located, catalogue correction, scope disagreement, partial disclosure, delay or wording-only; record alternative explanations and falsification tests.
Assess complaint eligibility separately for each body: jurisdiction, prerequisite, limitation, evidence, remedy and proportionality; prepare only where the threshold is met.

global_work_packages.name: Master question bank and missing-question analysis
tasks: Create master QID register with source lead, importance, institution, record family, date span, aliases, requested output and answer test.
Compare every 2026 request, response, refusal, clarification, review, complaint and Q&A item to identify questions not asked or only partly answered.
Run independent red-team review: who else may hold it, which predecessor/successor body existed, what record could disprove the working hypothesis and what alternative route remains.

global_work_packages.name: Operational speed and follow-up
tasks: Create next-working-day inbox triage and due-date controls with named owner and backup.
Enforce one-working-day routine drafting and review target; report every exception with a reason and recovery date.
Create 5/2/0-day reminders, next-working-day overdue chase, and 5/10-working-day escalation review where proportionate.
Run weekly sweep of sent mail, drafts, HubSpot tasks, statutory clocks, complaints, preservation notices and unanswered QIDs.

global_work_packages.name: Independent quality and reporting
tasks: Every task has a testable acceptance criterion, source links, evidence date, reviewer and result.
Weekly dashboard separates statutory clock performance, authority delay, requester delay, unanswered questions, unread attachments, drafts waiting and complaint eligibility.
Monthly PRINCE2 highlight report: RAG, products accepted, tolerance forecast, top risks/issues, decisions needed, stage progress and lessons.

global_work_packages.name: Records destruction, loss and custody audit
tasks: For every destroyed/lost/not-held statement, seek disposal schedule, authority, date, method, transfer, incident report, inventory and audit trail where held.
Search alternative repositories and predecessor bodies; distinguish never-created, destroyed, transferred, miscatalogued, unlocated and withheld.
Preserve every version of catalogue descriptions, search statements, correspondence and disclosure decisions.

global_work_packages.name: Dartboard roadmap and per-recipient ladder audit
tasks: Reconcile all 84 unique Dartboard roadmap lane IDs and 924 escalation steps against the 86 subprojects; preserve lane IDs and the original 21 November snapshot.

For each lane, verify every step's legal basis, recipient policy, prerequisite, deadline, source URL and check date; classify statutory, good-practice, discretionary, parallel, unavailable or not applicable.
Retain the recipient-specific ladder; do not substitute one institution's route for another's.

global_work_packages.name: Exhaustive alternative-options sweep
tasks: For every unanswered question, list all plausible record holders, predecessor/successor bodies, archive deposits, contractors, published catalogues and third-party custodians.
Assess FOIA, EIR, SAR, law-enforcement access, court-record access, land-register copies, archive reading room, voluntary enquiry and regulator/ombudsman processes.
Record why every route is used, deferred, unavailable or disproportionate; no route is silently omitted.

global_work_packages.name: 2026 withdrawals and live carryovers
tasks: Preserve the 18 requester-initiated closures from 19 November as a separate status; do not erase earlier clock results or count them as institutional non-response.
Reconcile each live 2026 carryover, including ICO, HMLR, MoJ, NPCC, Museum Wales and preservation notices, before issuing a repeat request.
For each closed/withdrawn lane, decide whether a fresh 2027 request is needed, what gap it answers and how it differs from the withdrawn request.

global_work_packages.name: PRINCE2 initiation and work-package authority
tasks: Approve the 2027 PID, continued business case, Project Board roles, project approach, stage plan and product descriptions before delivery starts.
Set time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability tolerances; define exception thresholds and decision rights.
Issue a signed work-package instruction for every task group with owner, reviewer, dependencies, acceptance test, evidence outputs and due dates.

global_work_packages.name: Evidence ingestion and scope integrity
tasks: Ingest each incoming disclosure and attachment into the evidence library within one working day with stable evidence ID, source, date, version, page count and checksum where available.
Reconcile all pages and attachments against the response schedule; flag missing pages, unreadable scans, missing annexes and unexplained redactions.
Preserve the full scope of site-wide and multi-record requests; log any narrowing, its reason, the decision-maker and independent QA approval.

global_work_packages.name: Highlight-report discipline and product acceptance
tasks: Produce a weekly highlight report with actuals, forecast, tolerance status, product acceptance, requester response latency, authority delay and unresolved decisions.
Run a daily unsent-draft sweep and a weekly product/evidence ingestion sweep; no draft or disclosure remains unowned.
Do not report an activity as a completed product; record the acceptance test, reviewer, evidence and any outstanding defect.

acceptance_criteria: Output saved with stable identifier and version.
Every factual statement linked to a source or explicitly marked unverified.
Result checked against complete correspondence and relevant attachments.
No duplicate request, unsupported allegation or unauthorised external action.
task_defaults.completion_rule: Complete only when output exists, sources are cited, the question is answered or disposition justified, contradictions are recorded, independent QA passes and next action is set.

carryovers.action: Check response on the next working day; preserve the request and exact due-date calculation.
Reconcile current position and route; do not assume the earlier status remains unchanged.
Check the ironwork-statement search and every attachment; record exact answer.
Reconcile case stage, requested evidence, response date and next action.
Reconcile application, evidence and decision route.

carryovers.status: Advice route live at 21 November snapshot
carryovers.action: Reconcile advice scope and whether a separate complaint is required.
Keep separate from FOI/EIR, SAR, ICR and any withdrawn voluntary enquiry.
Reconcile exact current status and any requester closure before further action.
Verify receipt, scope, response, custodian and continuing preservation need.

open.question: When and how did the Bute Estate acquire Great House from the Vaughans?
open.answer: Bute bought the lordship of the manor in 1793. The heritage record says Bute acquired the freehold of Great House in the early 19th century. The conveyance from the Vaughans or their heirs has not been located, so the date, the price and any leases it recited are unknown.
next: NLW Bute Estate Records: the Vaughan conveyance and abstract of title
Mount Stuart: Bute estate deeds (research visit)

open.question: Who was involved in the eviction and demolition of 30 November – 6 December 1988?
open.answer: Press reports record the eviction on 30 November and demolition from about 4am on 6 December 1988 by BP Properties. South Wales Police reported no records under FOI 719/26 (internal review 1188/26); on FOI 1264/26 (operational records) the force asked on 13 Oct 2026 for the names of individuals or entities involved, and suspended the clock under s.10(6) until clarified. The MOD relied on section 23(5) for the Special Forces element of FOI2026/09019 and reported nothing in scope on the SAR.
next: SWP FOI 1264/26: send the clarification (BP Properties Ltd, its agents and contractors, the bailiffs, the family) so the clock restarts
MOD internal review DPR2026/46503
RCAHMW: Suggett's post-demolition visit, Archive 6048945

open.question: Where is Mary Doreen Williams's death registration (1983)?
open.answer: FreeBMD indexes a 1983 death. The Vale of Glamorgan and Cardiff register offices both report not holding the registration (30 Sep and 12 Oct 2026); Cardiff has passed the search on.
next: Cardiff Register Office onward search (13 Oct 2026 reply)

open.question: What does the 1910 Valuation Office survey record for Great House?
open.answer: The National Archives identified the Valuation Office map for OS Glamorgan XLVII.6 (12 Oct 2026). The field book (DVAL/1/33 per Glamorgan Archives) would record owner, occupier and hereditament for 1910, which would show whether the house and fields were then valued as one unit or two.
next: Order the IR 58 / map copy for XLVII.6 and the field book entry

open.question: What rights and land were affected by the 1905 Bute–Cardiff Corporation conveyance and the 1924 Bute–Corbett drain agreement?
open.answer: The existing title-history catalogue identifies a Bute–Cardiff Corporation conveyance dated 23 February 1905 (EV-0013) and a Bute–James Pelham Stuart Corbett agreement dated 15 May 1924 concerning construction and maintenance of a drain (EV-0015). The register descriptions are leads only: the original deeds and plans have not yet been examined. They do not establish that Cardiff Corporation or Corbett acquired the freehold, occupied a defined site, or obtained title by adverse possession. The 1916 Bute–John Williams yearly tenancy (EV-0014), described in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 as covering 'the whole farm', is relevant counter-evidence to any claim that Bute had already disposed of the entire holding.
next: Obtain the complete 1905 conveyance and all plans; identify whether it granted an easement, conveyed a defined site, or did both
Locate deposited plans and contemporary records for the Western Sewer and any pumping-station compound; plot the route against Great House Farm parcels
Obtain the original 1916 tenancy and plan, if extant, and establish whether any infrastructure site was excluded
Obtain the 15 May 1924 drain agreement and plan; compare its parties, route and land with the 1905 instrument
Identify the 1961 deed and the exact parcel and instrument relied on in the later first-registration process

qa_research_questions.question: Which other recorded buildings stood within 200 m of the house, and do site files survive for them?
qa_research_questions.answer:
The national record (Coflein) has four entries close to the house besides Great House Farm itself (NPRN 20182). NPRN 15342 is "Llandough, Remains of House At", a medieval house at ST 1682 7320, about 110 m south of the house. NPRN 19886 is Rose Cottage, a later 17th-century house at ST 1674 7320, ruinous when surveyed in 1964 and since demolished, about 130 m to the south-west. NPRN 19159 is Llandough Grange, a post-medieval dwelling at ST 1685 7313, about 185 m to the south-south-east. NPRN 400051 is the Roman villa site at ST 1680 7330, excavated in 1979. The entries for 15342 and 19159 carry no description. Distances are worked from the grid references, which are given to 10 m.

Points for:
• Coflein NPRN 15342, 19159, 19886 and 400051 (read 13 November 2026)

Not yet established:
• Whether NPRN 15342 is the same medieval house remains reported south of the church in 1963 and 1979
• Which of these stood on the house parcel, the fields parcel or neither

Records still to check:
• The National Monuments Record site files behind NPRN 15342, 19159 and 19886 (an enquiry is drafted, not sent)
• The tithe map and apportionment, for the plot numbers under each grid reference

qa_research_questions.question: What do the Mathew family papers show about Llandough and Leckwith holdings before the Bute estate?
qa_research_questions.answer:
Glamorgan Archives holds the papers of the Mathew family of Radyr and Llandaff (DMAT). The published list runs to DMAT 206–207. It records a Vaughan holding in the manor of Leckwith in 1682, other owners granting land there in 1715, 1729 and 1734, and Mathews "of Llandough" through the 18th century. A later item, DMAT/279, is a late 18th-century plan of "Ty Mawr farm, Llandough [Gedrych property]" (photocopy; catalogue record MED-0208).

Points for:
• DMAT 168: surrender and admission of Morris Vaughan to a tenement and land in the manor of Leckwith, November 1682
• DMAT 177: Thomas, Viscount Windsor, conveys a cottage and land in the manor of Leckwith to Lewis Morgan of Leckwith, yeoman, 7 and 8 December 1715
• DMAT 170 and 171: a cottage and land near Leckwith church, leased by the Dowager Countess of Pembroke on 23 October 1729; a 99-year lease at the Manor of Leckwith Court and Audit, 5 December 1734
• DMAT 2, 7, 60, 187 and 189: Anthony Mathew of Llandough (will, 1740), William Mathew of Llandough (leases, 1770 and 1774), William John of Llandough, farmer (marriage bond, 1774), John Mathew of Llandough (inventory, 1805)
• DMAT 69: copy entries from the Leckwith, Llandough and Michaelston-le-Pit parish registers
• DMAT 175–176: William Gedrych of Leckwith, with Leckwith Farm in his occupation, 1829; DMAT 53: Gedrych v. Mathew, 1829

Not yet established:
• Which Llandough the Mathew entries mean. DMAT 69 groups Llandough with Leckwith and Michaelston-le-Pit, which points to Llandough near Penarth; the list does not state it
• Whether Morris Vaughan of 1682 belongs to the Vaughan family recorded at Great House
• Which land the "Gedrych property" plan covers, and where the original plan is held

A name to keep apart: "Great House" in these papers is usually the Mathew family's house at Whitchurch, a different place.

Records still to check:
• The list for DMAT 208 onwards, and the catalogue entry for DMAT/279 (an enquiry is drafted, not sent)
• DMAT 168, 171 and 177 themselves

sources.label: Glamorgan Archives DMAT list (The National Archives, Discovery)

qa_research_questions.question: Do the Plymouth (Windsor) estate plans show the boundary with the Great House holding?
qa_research_questions.answer:
Three plans in the Plymouth estate collection at Glamorgan Archives (DPL) cover Llandough before and at the time of the tithe survey. None has been seen yet. A plan of a neighbouring estate marks its own edge, so these may show where the Windsor and Clive lands stopped and who held the land next to them.

Points for:
• DPL/6: plan of Lord Plymouth's estates in Penarth, Llandough, Cogan and Lavernock, about 1768
• DPL/7: rough sketch maps, about 1820–1840, including a tracing for Llandough
• DPL/8: plan of Lady H. Clive's lands in Cogan and Llandough parishes, about 1840

Not yet established:
• Whether any of the three reaches the land beside St Dochdwy's Church
• Whether the neighbouring owners and occupiers are named on them

Records still to check:
• DPL/6, DPL/7 and DPL/8 (an enquiry on copying is drafted, not sent)
• The Plymouth rentals and abstract of leases for Glamorgan, 1712–1797, in the same collection

sources.label: Glamorgan Archives DPL list (The National Archives, Discovery)

qa_research_questions.question: What has Welsh Government published about the 1988 Cadw inspection?
qa_research_questions.answer:
Welsh Government published its response to request ATISN 27021 on its disclosure log, dated 11 June 2026. It records that Cadw inspectors visited and assessed the house and that it did not meet the criteria for listing. The only record it holds is two inspection photographs, of the house and of the barn, dated 29 July 1988. It holds nothing else for 1970–1999, and records that other papers would have gone to the Royal Commission (RCAHMW) or been destroyed under the Public Records Act 1958.

Points for:
• Welsh Government disclosure log, ATISN 27021, 11 June 2026

Not yet established:
• The inspectors' written assessment, and the date and authority for the disposal of the 1988 file

Records still to check:
• RCAHMW, for anything received from Cadw or the Welsh Office in 1988–89
• The replies to ATISN 26-0009 and 26-0075, listed in the hall

qa_research_questions.question: What did the Ministry of Defence state about armed forces involvement in 1988?
qa_research_questions.answer:
The Ministry of Defence replied to request FOI2026/09019 on 29 May 2026, and the reply is published on WhatDoTheyKnow. For Special Forces it relied on section 23(5) of the Freedom of Information Act and would neither confirm nor deny that information is held, adding that this is no indication either way. For the rest of the request (military aid to the civil authorities, and correspondence with the police, the council and the Welsh Office) it stated that no information is held. It pointed to The National Archives at Kew for unit historical records and commanders' diaries of the period.

Points for:
• Ministry of Defence reply, FOI2026/09019, 29 May 2026

Not yet established:
• Which record systems and date ranges were searched for the part reported as not held

Records still to check:
• The National Archives: unit historical records and commanders' diaries for late 1988
• The internal review of FOI2026/09019, listed in the hall

qa_research_questions.question: Where did Marconi stay during the May 1897 trials, and who was the Mr Williams at Lavernock?
qa_research_questions.answer:
The family account is that Marconi lodged at Great House during the trials and that a Mr Williams of the house helped with a horse and cart. No record made at the time and naming the house has been found yet. A 1993 journal article puts Marconi's headquarters for the trials at the Penarth Hotel, with the trials at Lavernock Point between 6 and 29 May 1897. The Evening Express of 15 May 1897, as transcribed in a 2019 local history article, names "Mr Williams (of the engineering department, Cardiff)" as fixing a 120-foot pole at Lavernock Point. That is a second Williams at the trials, so the two must not be merged.

Points for:
• The family account, repeated in the 1974 press reports

Points against:
• BIAS Journal 26 (1993): headquarters at the Penarth Hotel
• Post Office Limited, FOI2026/00751: no record held of a Mr Williams and the 1897 experiments

Not yet established:
• Where Marconi's assistants and the Post Office staff lodged
• Whether the Mr Williams of the newspaper report was a Post Office engineer with no link to the house

Records still to check:
• The Evening Express page of 15 May 1897 itself (Welsh Newspapers Online)
• George Kemp's diaries for May 1897 (Marconi Archives, Bodleian Library)

qa_research_questions.question: What rights did the 1905 and 1924 drainage instruments grant over land associated with Great House Farm?
qa_research_questions.answer: The title-history schedule identifies a Bute–Cardiff Corporation conveyance dated 23 February 1905 (EV-0013) and a Bute–James Pelham Stuart Corbett agreement dated 15 May 1924 for construction and maintenance of a drain (EV-0015). The original instruments and plans have not yet been examined. The register descriptions alone do not establish a freehold transfer, exclusive occupation or adverse possession. The 1916 Bute–John Williams yearly tenancy (EV-0014), described in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 as covering 'the whole farm', is relevant counter-evidence to any suggestion that Bute had already disposed of the entire holding.
